merger_name: AngloGold Ashanti Australia – Matsa Lake Carey tenements
merger_description:
In February 2025, AngloGold Ashanti Australia Limited (**AGA Australia**) entered into a tenements option agreement (**Option Agreement**) with Matsa Gold Pty Ltd (**Matsa Gold**) and Red October Gold Pty Ltd (**Red October Gold**) in relation to certain tenements at Matsa Resources Limited's (**Matsa Resources**) Lake Carey Gold Project. AGA Australia has since withdrawn several tenements from the Option Agreement that relate to Matsa Gold and Red October Gold’s existing operations at the Lake Carey Gold Project. The five tenements that remain subject to the Option Agreement (the **Tenements**) do not relate to any existing gold mine.

AGA Australia proposes to exercise the option (**Option**) in the Option Agreement to acquire the Tenements and be assigned certain associated access and royalty contracts related to the Tenements (the **Acquisition**). The purpose of AGA Australia exercising the Option is to allow AGA Australia to carry out exploration for gold in the area subject to the Tenements.

AGA Australia is a gold mining company operating in Australia. It owns the Sunrise Dam gold mine and has a 70% interest in and manages the Tropicana gold mine, both of which are located in Western Australia.

AGA Australia is a subsidiary of AngloGold Ashanti plc (**AGA**). AGA is a global gold mining company with a diverse, high-quality portfolio of operations, projects and exploration activities across ten countries. AGA is incorporated in England and Wales, headquartered in Denver, Colorado (USA), and has a primary listing on the New York Stock Exchange and secondary listings on the Johannesburg and Ghana Stock Exchanges.

Matsa Gold and Red October Gold are wholly owned subsidiaries of Matsa Resources, an ASX-listed gold mining company with operations in Western Australia and Thailand.

events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
AngloGold Ashanti Australia Limited (AGA Australia) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of certain
tenements related to Matsa Resources Limited’s (Matsa Resources)
Lake Carey Gold Project, as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, AGA Australia, is a gold mining company operating in
Australia. It owns the Sunrise Dam gold mine and has a 70% interest
in (and manages) the Tropicana gold mine, both of which are located
in Western Australia.
AGA Australia is a subsidiary of AngloGold Ashanti plc (AGA). AGA is
a global gold mining company with a diverse portfolio of operations,
projects, and exploration activities across 10 countries. AGA is
incorporated in England and Wales, headquartered in Denver,
Colorado (USA), and has a primary listing on the New York Stock
Exchange and secondary listings on the Johannesburg and Ghana
Stock Exchanges.
AGA Australia proposes to exercise the option in a tenements option
agreement (Option Agreement) entered into in February 2025 with
Matsa Gold Pty Ltd (Matsa Gold) and Red October Gold Pty Ltd (Red
October Gold) in relation to certain tenements at Matsa Resources’
Lake Carey Gold Project. AGA Australia has since withdrawn several
tenements from the Option Agreement that relate to Matsa Gold and
Red October Gold’s existing operations at the Lake Carey Gold
Project. The five tenements that remain subject to the Option
Agreement (the Tenements) do not relate to any existing gold mine.
The purpose of AGA Australia exercising the option is to allow it to
carry out exploration for gold in the area subject to the Tenements.
Matsa Gold and Red October Gold are wholly owned subsidiaries of
Matsa Resources, an ASX-listed gold mining company with
operations in Western Australia and Thailand.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the increment in share of the actual and expected
production and supply of gold in Australia and globally
arising from the Acquisition is expected to be small
b. there are alternative producers and suppliers of gold in
Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
